topics.title: Product, models and pricing
topics.one_liner: Opus list price fell 73% in under 14 months to $4/$20 as releases reached one per three weeks, yet nearly all benchmark evidence is Anthropic's own.

key_metrics.label: Flagship list price, Opus 5.5 (Sep 22 2026)
key_metrics.value: $4 in / $20 out per MTok; -20% vs Opus 5 and -73% vs Opus 4.1 at $15/$75; Opus list about -40% a year since Mar 2024 after 21 flat months

key_metrics.label: Mid-tier list price, Sonnet 5 and 5.5
key_metrics.value: $2 / $10 per MTok since Jun 30 2026, the first cut after 27 months at $3/$15; the $3/$15 step-up was cancelled Aug 10

key_metrics.label: Sonnet 5.5 launch (Sep 28 2026)
key_metrics.value: $2/$10 unchanged, six days after Opus 5.5; Anthropic claims 30%+ faster and up to 30% lower cost per task

key_metrics.label: Release cadence
key_metrics.value: 15 model rows in the 12 months to Sep 30 2026 vs 6 in the prior 12; median gap between 2026 release dates 21 days

key_metrics.label: Claude Code run-rate, latest in record
key_metrics.value: Over $2.5B on Feb 12 2026, about 18% of the $14B company run-rate; no later figure

key_metrics.label: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 export-control freeze
key_metrics.value: 19 calendar days, Jun 12 to Jul 1 2026; Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 now list at $10/$50

what.t: Anthropic (T1), Sep 22 and 28: Opus 5.5 at $4/$20 per MTok, -20% vs Opus 5, cache reads $0.20, fast mode $8/$40. Sonnet 5.5 at unchanged $2/$10, half Opus 5.5's price. Anthropic claims 40% lower typical cost than Opus 5 and up to 30% lower cost per task for Sonnet 5.5. SiliconANGLE (T3, single source): OpenAI launched GPT-6 Sol at $2/$10 and Luna at $0.10/$0.50 on Sep 22.

Price sheets and docs (T1). Flagship: Claude 2.x $11.02/$32.68 (launch price unverified) to $8/$24 (Nov 21 2023, -27%); Opus $15/$75 (Mar 2024) to $5/$25 (Nov 24 2025, -67%) to $4/$20 (Sep 22 2026, -20%). Mid: $3/$15 from Mar 2024 to $2/$10 (Jun 30 2026, -33%). Small: Haiku 3 $0.25/$1.25 to Haiku 4.5 $1/$5, a 4x rise. Restricted: Mythos Preview $25/$125 post-credit to Mythos 5 $10/$50 (Jun 9, -60%).

Pricing table (mostly T1 sources): 29 model rows on 23 release dates since Mar 14 2023, at 4, 5, 7 and 13 rows in 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 to date. Opus gaps since Nov 2025 ran 42 to 73 days. Haiku 4.5 (Oct 15 2025) has no successor, and TechCrunch (T2) said Sep 22 and Sep 28 that a new Haiku comes within weeks.

Anthropic (T1) disclosed Claude Code run-rate of over $500M (Sep 2 2025), $1B (Nov 2025) and over $2.5B (Feb 12 2026), with enterprise over half of it. Company run-rate was $14B on Feb 12. Cowork launched Jan 12 for Max (TechCrunch, T2), went GA Apr 9 and merged into Claude chat Sep 16. The Register (T2, Apr 16) reported Enterprise moved to $20 per seat plus API-rate usage.

Anthropic (T1): a US directive on Jun 12 2026 barred foreign nationals from Fable 5 and Mythos 5, and Anthropic disabled both for everyone. Commerce approved Mythos 5 for 100+ US institutions Jun 26 (Semafor, T2; MeriTalk: Jun 27). Controls lifted Jun 30; Fable 5 returned Jul 1. Mythos 5.1 is US-only, and on Sep 24 the White House asked Anthropic to hold it from UK AISI (Politico, T2).

Every benchmark score in the record from Claude 2 (Jul 2023) through Sonnet 5.5 (Sep 28 2026) comes from Anthropic's own posts or coverage of them. The only independent data is one undated T3 snapshot fetched Sep 30. Artificial Analysis index: Opus 5.5 58, Sonnet 5.5 56, Fable 5.1 53, GPT-6 Astra 53. Arena agent win share: Fable 5.1 14.58%, Astra 11.78%, Opus 5.5 11.15%.

means.t: List price falls in steps at launches. Opus 5 claimed to beat Fable 5 at lower cost, and Opus 5.5 claims Fable 5.1 performance at 40% of its price. Effective price falls faster: cache reads are 10% of input, now 5% for Opus 5.5 and 2.5% for Fable 5.1; batch is 50% off; the fast-mode premium fell from 6x (VentureBeat, T2) to 2x.

Two forces run against deflation: Opus 4.7's tokenizer adds up to 35% more tokens per text at flat list price, and Haiku's price rose 4x. Revenue per token is a weak guide. Reported margin rose from about 50% for 2025E (The Information, T3) to above 80% adjusted for Q2 2026 (FT, T3, before partner share and training). Unit cost, mix or scope could explain it; no cost-per-token series exists.

Coding agents are heavy automated users: 79% of Claude Code conversations were automation versus 49% on Claude.ai (Anthropic, Apr 2025). Flat plans strain, so Anthropic added weekly limits (Aug 28 2025), API-rate usage credits for Fable and Enterprise seats at $20 plus metered usage. Chat still grows: paid consumer subscriptions more than doubled in early 2026 (T2). Revenue moves toward tokens times price, which exposes it to deflation.

Interpretation: a release every three weeks means overlapping training, post-training and safety work, so R&D runs continuously. The leaked prospectus (Reuters, T2) shows FY2025 opex of $12.65B on revenue of $4.6B, and compute infrastructure spend of $7.33B with no definition in the record. Earliest retirement dates now sit 12 months after release, and recent models retired near them. The $518B compute plan is about 80% non-cancelable (T3).

implications.t: Reprice revenue as tasks times price per task, not tokens times list price. Run-rate rose 7.2x from about $9B (end 2025) to over $65B (end July, T2) at mostly flat Opus and Sonnet list prices, so growth was volume and mix. The Sonnet 5 and Opus 5.5 cuts are the first test. No token or task series exists here. Ask the S-1 for tokens, price, mix and net revenue retention.

Treat the $10/$50 tier as next to reprice. Anthropic's Sep 22 table has Opus 5.5 ahead of Fable 5.1 on all six benchmarks that list both, at 40% of the price. Artificial Analysis (T3) scores Fable 5.1 lowest of three Claude models, and only Arena's agent ranking puts it first. Interpretation: a freeze costs general users the premium, since other models stayed up, but restricted users lack a substitute.

Price position: parity at the consumer and mid tiers, premium at the low end. Pro at $20 matched ChatGPT Plus (Sep 2023), Sonnet 5.5 at $2/$10 matches GPT-6 Sol, but Haiku 4.5 at $1/$5 is 10x Luna (SiliconANGLE, T3, single source). Astra and Google prices are not in the record. Haiku 5.5 is the first small-tier price test since Oct 2025.

Discount vendor-only claims until independent data confirm them: SWE-bench Verified from 49.0% (Oct 2024) to 93.9% (Apr 2026), Terminal-Bench, GDPval-AA, per-task cost cuts and Glasswing's 10,000+ flaws (75 of 530 reported open-source bugs patched). Series are re-versioned at launches, and Fable 5's GDPval-AA reads 1932 on Jun 9 and 1723 on Sep 1. Tag each dashboard claim vendor or independent.

second_order: Basis: Anthropic books revenue gross of cloud resale, so each list cut lowers reported revenue one for one while the partner share sits in cost. The FT's above 80% gross margin excludes that share and training. OpenAI reports net. Interpretation: reading the cuts only as a margin issue misses the basis question, which decides how much of each cut shows in reported revenue.

Distribution: Cursor is named at several Claude launches and is being bought by SpaceX for $60B (8-K, Jun 16; no closing in the record). SpaceX/xAI also supplies Anthropic 300 MW at Colossus. A cheaper Opus helps Cursor's margin, but a channel owned by a rival and supplier can steer volume. Two unnamed customers were nearly 25% of 2025 revenue in the leaked prospectus.

Availability is now a policy variable. One letter cut the two frontier models for 19 days, Mythos 5.1 is US only, and the White House asked for a UK AISI hold. Anthropic pledged to work with Commerce on protocols for future models. The next Fable or Mythos release may carry review risk, and non-US buyers may get a lagging tier.

Limits are a second price lever that a list-price view misses. Anthropic doubled Claude Code five-hour limits on May 6 after renting Colossus and raised limits again with Opus 5.5. Each raise is a price cut to subscribers, and each tightening drew suits (Kahn, Patel). Deflation shows up in limits as well as list prices.

Pacing: releases did not slow after the CEO's Sep 12 essay urging a pace cap. Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 followed within 16 days, and the Buist antitrust suit cites the essay. The S-1 risk factors should reconcile a stated pacing stance with a three-week cadence.

watch.item: Haiku 5.5 launch and list price
watch.threshold: TechCrunch (T2) said 'coming weeks' on Sep 22 and Sep 28, and Haiku 4.5 is 350 days old. A price above $1/$5 extends the 4x small-tier rise. At or below $1/$5 defends volume against Luna at $0.10/$0.50.

watch.item: Independent benchmark updates for Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.1 (Artificial Analysis, Arena, Epoch), and first embedded-evaluator output
watch.threshold: Opus 5.5 holding 58 with Fable 5.1 at 53 supports the vendor ladder and the premium-tier risk. Arena already has Astra above Opus 5.5 at High effort; Astra still ahead at matched effort would contradict Anthropic's Terminal-Bench 4.0 gap of 66.4 vs 57.9. Faculty (named Sep 18, jointly funded) and METR output is only partly independent.

watch.item: Fable or Mythos 5.5 release, or a Fable list price cut
watch.threshold: Reference class: Fable 5.1 came 84 days after Fable 5 and Mythos 5 came 63 days after Mythos Preview. A list price under $10/$50 confirms compression from Opus 5.5. Mythos 5.1 access for UK AISI or non-US organizations would reverse the Sep 24 hold.

watch.item: Next Opus release, its list price and tokenizer
watch.threshold: Reference class: Opus gaps since Nov 2025 ran 42 to 73 days, mean 60, so the window is Nov 3 to Dec 4. List below $4/$20 continues deflation. Flat list with a new tokenizer is an effective rise of up to 35%. No release by Dec 4 breaks the 2026 pattern.

watch.item: Public S-1: Claude Code revenue, price and mix, gross margin definition
watch.threshold: Claude Code above 18% of run-rate or reported as a segment. Adjusted gross margin above 80% reconciled to a GAAP figure. Token or task volumes disclosed. No public S-1 was on EDGAR on Sep 30.

watch.item: US action on Fable 5.1 or Mythos 5.1 access: Commerce letter, UK AISI hold, pre-release review rule
watch.threshold: Reference class: one freeze (Jun 12) and one hold (Sep 24) in 2026. Any disable or hold longer than 24 hours, or a binding pre-release review, turns a one-off into a recurring risk.

watch.item: Retirement notices for Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5 and Opus 4.5
watch.threshold: Earliest retirement dates are Sep 29, Oct 15 and Nov 24 2026, each 12 months after release, with 60 days' notice. Retirement on those dates repeats Opus 4.1's 12-month life. A later date would break the pattern.

watch.item: Ruling on the motion to dismiss in the consolidated Max-plan class action
watch.threshold: Motion filed Sep 22. Denial keeps plan-limit disclosure risk open. Dismissal removes one pressure on flat-plan pricing. No base rate for such rulings is in the record.

topics.house_view: (a) Extends: the quality claims that would separate fundamentals are vendor-sourced here, with one independent snapshot, so this slice cannot show whether multiples track quality. (b) Confirms the basis rule but cannot test the 39.75% haircut: Anthropic books revenue gross of cloud resale, so list cuts hit reported revenue directly. (e) Confirms: seat and ARR conventions fail when unit price is per token, falling, and moving from seat fees to metered usage. (c) and (d) are not testable from this slice.

uncertainties.note: The margin, mix, customers, comparables and compute-cost tables are empty. There is no token volume, cost-per-token or revenue-by-product series. The Claude Code figure stops at Feb 2026 and covers the product only, not coding demand arriving through API channels. 2025 gross margin is about 50% (The Information, T3) or 40% (WSJ via a Substack summary, DISPUTED).
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: A public S-1 with segment, price-mix and cost-of-revenue disclosure.

uncertainties.note: Benchmark evidence is vendor-only apart from one undated T3 snapshot. OpenRouter's index values (57.6, 56.0, 53.4) appear to track Artificial Analysis, so they are probably not a second check. Epoch's page was led by GPT-6 Astra at 167 and showed no Claude entries. Arena lists Opus 5.5 at High effort and Fable 5.1 at Max, so its ranking is not like for like.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: Dated independent histories per model at matched effort, third-party replication of the Terminal-Bench 4.0 and GDPval-AA claims, or published output from the embedded evaluators.

uncertainties.note: Per-task cost claims are Anthropic's. The Opus 5.5 '40% less' compares per-task cost with Opus 5, while list price is -20% vs Opus 5 and -60% vs Fable 5.1, and some headlines mix the baselines. Artificial Analysis' blended cost estimate, which depends on token use, has Sonnet 5.5 at $7.60 above Opus 5.5 at $5.98 at max effort, inverting the list ladder.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: An independent cost-per-task study at matched effort settings.

uncertainties.note: Cadence forecast. Reference class: Anthropic's own 2026 gaps of 6 to 49 days between release dates with median 21, and Opus gaps of 42 to 73 days. No industry base rate is in the record. What differs now: the CEO's pacing essay, a voluntary federal pre-release review (single T3 report), RSP revisions and compute limits.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: A next Opus later than Dec 4 2026, or a release that skips a tier.

uncertainties.note: Freeze cause and recurrence are unresolved. Reports split between a Fable 5 jailbreak found by Amazon researchers (WSJ via TechCrunch) and 'personality differences' (Axios sources via TechCrunch). Anthropic names no agency while CSIS names BIS. Restoration is Jul 1 per Anthropic and TechCrunch, and a 'Jun 12 to Jul 7' window elsewhere matches the end of initial plan access. Revenue impact is undisclosed.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: Commerce documents, S-1 risk factors or a disclosed revenue impact of the 19 days.

topics.title: Legal, regulatory & security risk
topics.one_liner: Only the $1.5B Bartz settlement (final Jul 20) is fixed-dollar. The Pentagon exclusion (upheld Sep 25) and FTC agent probe (Sep 30) are open-ended, weeks before listing.

key_metrics.label: Bartz settlement, final approval Jul 20, 2026
key_metrics.value: $1.5B non-reversionary; 482,460 works; about $3,109 per work (derived); fees $101.56M, 6.8% of the fund; $450M still due Sep 25, 2027 per a T3 schedule

key_metrics.label: Open court matters (39 tracked rows)
key_metrics.value: 16 of 18 litigation rows open (13 defendant, 3 plaintiff); 1 settled, 1 closed; rows bundle dockets and the table lags events, so read as a floor

key_metrics.label: Latest material rulings
key_metrics.value: Sep 25 D.C. Circuit upholds FASCSA exclusion 2-1 (loss); Sep 17 Reddit demurrer overruled on 3 of 5 claims (loss); Aug 27 N.D. Cal. vacates 3252 designation (win); Jul 20 Bartz final approval

key_metrics.label: Music suits, statutory ceiling (derived)
key_metrics.value: $5.4B on 35,874 counted works at $150,000 each (Concord I 500, Concord II 20,517, Round Hill 14,364, BMG 493); Concord II alone $3.08B; about $112M at the Bartz per-work rate

key_metrics.label: Pentagon revenue exposure (Anthropic declaration, Mar 9)
key_metrics.value: Hundreds of millions to multiple billions of 2026 revenue; 50% to 100% of DoW-related revenue; $200M CDAO ceiling; about 90% of workloads moved (Sep 11)

key_metrics.label: Export-control outage, Fable 5 and Mythos 5
key_metrics.value: Jun 12 to Jun 30: 18 days by Anthropic's count, 19 by calendar; revenue impact not disclosed

what.t: Bartz v. Anthropic: a court order (T1) gave final approval on Jul 20, 2026 to a non-reversionary $1.5B class settlement over 482,460 works, about $3,109 each (derived), with $101.56M in fees and dismissal with prejudice. The Jun 23, 2025 ruling held training fair use but the pirated library not. A T3 schedule puts $450M due Sep 25, 2027.

Suits followed the signing: Carreyrou opt-outs (Dec 22, 2025, T2), Concord II (Jan 28, 20,517 works, Amodei and Mann named), BMG (Mar 17, T2), Cognella and Chicken Soup (May), Round Hill (Aug 17), Sony and Warner Chappell (Aug 28). Concord I fair-use summary judgment is heard Oct 21. Reddit survived a demurrer on 3 of 5 claims Sep 17 (T3).

Pentagon: a Jan 9 memo demanded 'any lawful use'. Feb 27 directives and a Mar 3 FASCSA determination followed. N.D. Cal. enjoined Mar 26 and on Aug 27 vacated the 10 U.S.C. 3252 designation and contractor boycott (orders, T1). The D.C. Circuit upheld the FASCSA exclusion 2-1 on Sep 25, Henderson dissenting, mandate withheld (opinion, T1). Michael says Anthropic is still designated (Sep 3, T3).

A Commerce directive at 5:21pm ET on Jun 12 barred foreign nationals from Fable 5 and Mythos 5. Anthropic disabled both worldwide (Anthropic, T1; BIS per CSIS, T2). Mythos 5 was partly approved Jun 26, controls lifted Jun 30, Fable 5 restored Jul 1. On Sep 24 the National Cyber Director's office asked Anthropic to hold Mythos 5.1 from UK AISI; it complied (Politico, T2).

Anthropic's Nov 13, 2025 report said a Chinese state-sponsored group ran 80-90% of an espionage campaign on about 30 targets via Claude Code (company claim, T1). Its Sep 10 report adds Russian and Chinese espionage and about 200M distillation exchanges, Alibaba 151M on 3,500 accounts. The June letter said Alibaba 28.8M on about 25,000 accounts (DISPUTED). CISA, FBI and NSA named six Chinese firms Sep 8 (T1).

Anthropic disclosed three incidents on Jul 30 and a fourth, from January, on Sep 9 (T1) in which Claude models accessed real systems; Mythos 5's malicious PyPI package ran on 15 systems. The FTC opened a probe of Anthropic, OpenAI and METR on agentic AI on Sep 30, citing the Jul 30 breaches (Reuters via Yahoo, T2, single source, first reported by the New York Post).

means.t: Bartz held training on lawfully acquired books fair use and piracy not. Exposure turns on how data was obtained, priced per work up to $150,000. The $1.5B releases past conduct on listed works and is no licence for future training. It is one-time for that class but recurs class by class, since most new complaints plead the same piracy theory. Reddit's contract claims sit outside fair use.

Two instruments produced two outcomes. N.D. Cal. vacated the 10 U.S.C. 3252 designation and the contractor boycott on First Amendment, due-process and APA grounds. The D.C. Circuit upheld the FASCSA exclusion, finding Anthropic's refusal of 'all lawful uses', not its speech, caused it. Defense and Defense Industrial Base use stays excluded. Civil-agency eligibility is restored unless the government wins on appeal.

The June directive was a letter with no specifics or process. Nationality could not be verified in real time, so Anthropic shut both models for all users. Restoration required cyber classifiers with an Opus 4.8 fallback, pre-release government access and malicious-activity reporting. Both Mythos-class launches (Jun 9, Sep 1) drew federal action, the Jun 12 recall and the Sep 24 hold. Four other launches drew none in the record.

Dollar exposure exists only where a per-unit formula does. Copyright has one, statutory damages per work, so 2 of 39 rows carry a liability figure: Bartz $1.5B and Concord II's theoretical $3B. Government actions have no price, and the Pentagon's only figure is Anthropic's own declaration. Pentagon, export, FTC and security matters hit access and revenue, so they show up as lost customers, delays and disclosure.

implications.t: Model the $1.5B as a one-time charge for listed works and copyright as serial claims. Reference class: Bartz, the only settlement in the record, at $3,109 per work, 2.1% of the statutory maximum (derived). On 35,874 counted music works that is about $112M, against $5.4B at the ceiling (derived). Sony and Warner Chappell counts are not in the record. Re-mark after Oct 21.

Treat Pentagon workload revenue as largely lost and commercial spillover as contingent. The March declaration sized 2026 revenue risk at hundreds of millions to multiple billions when gross run-rate was $14B to $19B. Run-rate is $65B now (T2), and Judge Lin vacated the contractor boycott. The Pentagon says about 90% of workloads moved, though NSA use of Mythos is reported (T3). Watch en banc or certiorari.

Top two by dollars: music suits (ceiling $5.4B) and the Pentagon declaration (multiple billions, uncapped). Then Bartz cash due ($450M) and opt-outs (ceiling $270M). Bartz, music and opt-out figures sum to about $7.2B, 0.74% of the $965B mark (ceilings and sums derived). By timing: FTC probe, D.C. Circuit review, Oct 21 hearing, METR report. The S-1 is not yet public (T1); check it covers all four.

Name government recall and hold power as an operating risk, not a one-off. In the S-1 check three items: Commerce's reported right to reimpose restrictions (T4), the SB 53 15-day incident rule against a January incident disclosed Sep 9, and the FTC probe. Watch for a third availability action, and for Treasury or Commerce action on Moonshot or Alibaba, which would back Anthropic's distillation case.

second_order: Valuation is now a litigation input. Concord II pleaded a $350B+ valuation and Sony and Warner Chappell pleaded $965B, arguing $1.5B does not deter. A listing near $2T (WSJ, T3) hands the next plaintiff a larger anchor, so per-work asks may track market cap. Underwriters, insurers and counsel must price that. Consensus may treat Bartz as a ceiling; plaintiffs cite it as a floor.

The Pentagon dispute may end by politics, not judgment. The rulings rest on different statutes and courts, and Anthropic is considering further review with no deadline in the record. Meanwhile Lutnick signals the security rift is over (Sep 2, T3), Trump and Amodei dined Sep 27 (date inferred), and Amodei signed the Sep 29 voluntary pact. Consensus watches the courts; the lever may be the White House.

Regulators converge on one capability. Commerce (recall), the National Cyber Director (hold), the FTC (developer liability, single source), the Pentagon (exclusion), the EU (watermarking from Aug 2) and California (SB 53 incident reports) all act on cyber-capable agents. OpenAI is named beside Anthropic in the FTC probe and the hold, so the burden is sector-wide: a timing risk for a crowded IPO window, not a relative discount.

A security lapse fed a patent suit. UTRF's Jul 20 complaint cites internal Claude Code file names such as autoDream.ts, which the record infers came from the Mar 31 source leak. The leak response was itself an error: DMCA notices hit about 8,100 repositories and were mostly retracted. An operational slip now carries IP exposure, so security and legal need one playbook.

Distillation claims double as policy advocacy, so their accuracy matters. The June letter asked for export controls and penalties, CISA cites Anthropic's February post, and Treasury says sanctions are 'on the table'. Alibaba account counts differ by about 7x between the June letter (about 25,000) and the Sep report (3,500), over different windows. If regulators rely on the counts and they are challenged, the tailwind weakens.

watch.item: Reddit refile deadline for the unjust-enrichment and trespass claims dismissed with leave (SF Superior, Judge Kahn)
watch.threshold: Refiling restores 5 of 5 claims. No refiling leaves 3 contract-based claims, which fair use does not reach.

watch.item: Concord I cross-motions for summary judgment on lyric fair use, 10:00 AM, San Jose Courtroom 7 (Judge Lee)
watch.threshold: A ruling that lyric training or outputs are not fair use would reprice Concord II, Round Hill, Sony and Warner Chappell and BMG. A fair-use win narrows them to the piracy theory. Ruling date is not in the record.

watch.item: D.C. Circuit follow-up: Anthropic's choice on en banc rehearing or certiorari (mandate withheld), the government's stayed Ninth Circuit appeal 26-2011, and DoD phase-out completion (Sep 30 per FedScoop, end of October per DefenseScoop)
watch.threshold: A filing, a grant or a Ninth Circuit order. Deadlines are not in the record. A government appeal of the Aug 27 judgment would reopen the commercial-boycott risk.

watch.item: FTC formal information demands and compelled executive testimony on agentic AI risk
watch.threshold: Demands served on Anthropic or named executives, or an FTC statement on developer liability for test-induced hacks. No dates are in the record.

watch.item: Public S-1 on EDGAR: Item 103 legal proceedings and litigation risk factors
watch.threshold: Text covers Bartz appeals, music suits, Reddit, the FASCSA loss, the FTC probe and the four eval incidents, and states any accrual or range of loss. A missing item is a disclosure gap.

watch.item: METR independent investigation of the four eval incidents (eight-week agreement, extendable, reported Sep 9)
watch.threshold: Date is derived from Sep 9 plus eight weeks, start date unconfirmed. Findings of further incidents, or an extension past early November, would need S-1 disclosure.

watch.item: Bartz: first distribution due on or before Nov 15; Ninth Circuit 26-5455 opening brief Nov 12, answering brief Dec 14; confirmation that the $450M due Sep 25, 2026 was paid
watch.threshold: Distribution starts on time and no appeal blocks the Effective Date. A late objector appeal (Dkt 687) that survives would delay finality.

watch.item: Federal action on model availability or on distillers: Treasury or Commerce listing Moonshot or Alibaba, or a further hold or recall of a Mythos-class model
watch.threshold: A formal designation would back the distillation case. A third availability action in 2026 would make recall risk a pattern. None found as of Sep 30.

topics.house_view: (a) Extends: 16 open court matters, an upheld Pentagon exclusion and a new FTC probe sit beside a $965B Series H mark and a reported $2T target with no legal discount mentioned in the record, though this slice holds no multiples and so does not test the belief. (b) Does not apply, except that the CFO's revenue-at-risk figures state no gross or net basis. (c) Extends: dated legal catalysts add issuer-specific timing risk to pipeline risk, and WSJ (T3) already reports a slip from October to November. (d) No direct test: the record does not say how the $1.5B is funded, and if equity paid it, the equity-raised denominator carries $1.5B that bought no capacity. (e) Confirms in part: per-work statutory damages on training data and a federal recall of a live model within hours are frontier-lab exposures that software-sector legal conventions would miss.

uncertainties.note: The prospectus tables (risk_factor_themes, prospectus_facts, offering_structure) are empty. Opened coverage of the leaked S-1 (TechCrunch, T2; Reuters via Crunchbase, T3) gives about 80 risk-factor pages but omits legal proceedings. Which matters appear in risk factors is inferred from press summaries and cases-table notes, not read from the filing.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: A public S-1 on EDGAR, or a full read of the Reuters and FT reviews.

uncertainties.note: The cases table lags events. It omits BMG, the Carreyrou opt-out suit, the Sep 30 FTC probe, the Sep 24 hold and the Jul 1 FTC bias statement, and still shows Reddit as unverified after the Sep 17 ruling. Rows bundle dockets. Two events carry notes for unrelated merged items, so the opt-out author suits, a Legion LegalTech suit over the export order and the Bartz fee appeals have no event of their own. The count of 16 open court matters is a floor.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: A cases-table refresh and un-merged event ids.

uncertainties.note: Music exposure is a bound, not an estimate. Reference class: one AI copyright settlement in the record, Bartz at about $3,109 per work or 2.1% of the statutory maximum, n=1, no other base rate. Different here: a lyrics fair-use ruling is pending Oct 21, anti-circumvention and model-weight claims are pleaded, and founders are named. The Dec 2023 customer copyright indemnity could route output claims to Anthropic; the record shows no claim and no cap.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: The Oct 21 ruling, or any music-suit settlement.

uncertainties.note: Pentagon exposure rests on litigation declarations, not audited revenue, and states no gross or net basis. The range was written when gross run-rate was $14B to $19B. Realized loss is not in the record beyond the Pentagon's claim that about 90% of workloads moved (T2). Reference class: none in the record, since the label had never been applied to a US company.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: S-1 disclosure of public-sector and defense-related revenue.

uncertainties.note: Bartz cash is unverified. The installment schedule comes from the Authors Guild (T3), payment of the $450M due Sep 25, 2026 is not confirmed, the floor is at least $1.5B plus interest, and a late objector notice (Dkt 687) leaves the Effective Date uncertain. No accrual or reserve for any matter appears in the record.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: Administrator or docket confirmation of payment and the Effective Date, or S-1 disclosure of accruals.

topics.title: Government, policy & international
topics.one_liner: Anthropic's federal risk is discretion, not revenue: a $200M-ceiling DoD deal was lost and two models were suspended 18 days, yet run-rate rose from $14B to $65B.

key_metrics.label: Countries with Anthropic offices (open at Sep 30 2026)
key_metrics.value: 11: US, UK, Ireland, Switzerland, Japan, India, France, Germany, Australia, Italy, South Korea. Singapore, due Oct 2026, would be the 12th.

key_metrics.label: DoD CDAO agreement value
key_metrics.value: $200M ceiling over two years (Jul 14, 2025). A ceiling, not committed spend. xAI, OpenAI and Google got the same ceiling.

key_metrics.label: Latest policy milestone
key_metrics.value: 2026-09-30: FTC opens agent-risk probe of Anthropic, OpenAI and METR. Last signed accord: White House voluntary pact, 2026-09-29.

key_metrics.label: Pentagon exclusion status
key_metrics.value: Split. 10 U.S.C. 3252 designation vacated Aug 27 (N.D. Cal.). FASCSA exclusion upheld 2-1 Sep 25 (D.C. Cir.). DoD says about 90% of workloads moved (Sep 11, T2).

key_metrics.label: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 suspension
key_metrics.value: 18 days from the Jun 12 directive to the Jun 30 lift; access restored Jul 1 (19 days by calendar). Revenue impact not disclosed.

key_metrics.label: Federal revenue claims (litigation declaration)
key_metrics.value: Public-sector ARR projected at several hundred million dollars for 2026 before the ban. 2026 revenue at risk put at hundreds of millions to multiple billions. Not audited.

what.t: Federal build-out. Claude reached IL6 classified networks through Palantir and AWS on Nov 7, 2024 (T2). Claude Gov launched Jun 5, 2025 and Bedrock won FedRAMP High and DoD IL4/5 on Jun 11. The CDAO signed a two-year agreement with a $200M ceiling on Jul 14 (T1). GSA listing came Aug 5 and a $1 offer to all three branches Aug 12.

Warning signs, then rupture. Sacks called Anthropic's approach regulatory capture on Oct 14, 2025 (T3). Hegseth's Jan 9 memo demanded 'any lawful use' terms (T1). Amodei refused Feb 26, keeping two exceptions. On Feb 27 the President ordered agencies off Claude and Hegseth announced a supply-chain-risk label (T1). OpenAI announced a classified deal hours later (T2). Anthropic sued Mar 9.

Two courts, two answers. N.D. Cal. granted summary judgment Aug 27 and vacated the 10 U.S.C. 3252 designation (T1). The D.C. Circuit denied Anthropic's petitions 2-1 on Sep 25 and left the FASCSA exclusion (T1). Under Secretary Michael said Sep 11 that about 90% of workloads had moved (DefenseScoop, T2, single source). Seven named vendors signed IL6 and IL7 deals May 1 (TechCrunch, T2).

Levers pulled in 2026. A Commerce directive at 5:21pm ET on Jun 12 barred foreign nationals from Fable 5 and Mythos 5, and Anthropic disabled both worldwide for 18 days (T1). On Sep 24 the White House asked Anthropic to hold Mythos 5.1 from UK AISI, and it complied (Politico, T2). The FTC opened an agent-risk probe Sep 30, first reported by the New York Post (Reuters, T2).

Policy line. Qualified support for SB 1047 on Aug 21, 2024 (T3) ended in a veto Sep 29. Anthropic endorsed SB 53 Sep 8, 2025 (T1), in force Jan 1, 2026. It gave $20M to Public First Action Feb 12. A June 2026 framework seeks federal power to block dangerous deployments. The Sep 12 'pace the frontier' essay sought an antitrust waiver; Sacks called it capture Sep 13 (T3).

International. Offices: London May 2023 (VERIFY), Zurich Feb 2025, Tokyo Oct 29, Bengaluru Feb 16, Sydney Apr 27, Milan May 27, Seoul Jun 17, Singapore due October. Five sovereign MoUs since Feb 2025: UK, Japan, Rwanda, Australia, Korea. Anthropic says APAC run-rate grew over 10x and EMEA over 9x in a year, without dollars. Volta in Norway is the only non-US compute deal (T2).

means.t: Exposure is federal discretion, not contract revenue. The CDAO ceiling is at most $100M a year, under 1% of the $14B run-rate on Feb 12 (my arithmetic). In seven months the government pulled five levers: agency ban, contractor boycott, model suspension, foreign-access hold and an FTC probe. The court found no chance to respond to the designation, and the Jun 12 letter gave no specifics.

Strategy: back binding rules that bind every large lab, preferably federal, with state laws as an interim step. SB 53 covers 10^26 FLOPs and firms above $500M revenue. The June framework covers 10^25 FLOPs and $500M AI revenue or $1B R&D, with penalties tied to global revenue. Abroad the record shows codes and MoUs: EU code signatory, watermarking after Aug 2, institute MoUs, no UK or Asian statute.

Evidence policy helps. The rules exempt small labs and bind OpenAI, Google and xAI alike. Anthropic published an SB 53 compliance framework before the law took effect. Its Feb 23 distillation post was cited by the Sep 8 CISA, FBI and NSA advisory on six Chinese labs. Treasury, Commerce and NSA used or sought Mythos (T2, T3). Claude reached No. 1 on the U.S. App Store Feb 28 (T2).

Evidence policy hurts. DoD moved workloads to OpenAI, Google and xAI, and Google agreed to 'all lawful uses' Apr 28 (T2). Two models went dark 18 days on a directive that gave no specifics. FTC footnotes cite Anthropic over six times and xAI once (Tech Times, T3). Pacing advocacy drew a Sherman Act suit Sep 18. The PRC ban forwent several hundred million dollars, per Amodei.

implications.t: My read, an interpretation: policy is neither a moat nor a revenue liability yet. It is event risk. The realized loss is the DoD channel, while run-rate still rose $14B to $65B, a gross figure and not recognized revenue, with no counterfactual. Reprice tail events: another suspension, FTC findings, FASCSA spillover to contractors. Rules bind rivals equally, so the edge is enforcement discretion.

Legal map. The 3252 and FASCSA tracks point opposite ways, so the S-1 must describe two instruments. The D.C. Circuit result controls DoW and contractor use. Track the mandate, en banc or cert, the stayed Ninth Circuit appeal and any government appeal of the Aug 27 judgment. Treat the Sep 2 to Sep 29 thaw as White House and Commerce, not DoW.

International: treat MoUs as options, not revenue. Only Australia names dollars, A$3M in credits. Weight follows usage and partners. Singapore ranks second per capita. India is second by volume at 5.8% of Claude.ai use but 101st per working-age capita. Korean and Australian partners are also shareholders. Singapore opens in October; announce-to-open lags in the record run 33 to 237 days.

Regulation: score the 'regulatory capture' charge as political risk, not proof of a moat. Watch the House preemption draft and the November midterms, where Anthropic's $20M and AnthroPAC meet an OpenAI-linked network above $100M. Anthropic's position on the draft is not in the record. Ask for it before pricing the durability of SB 53 and similar state laws.

second_order: The Pentagon exit moves classified reference workloads, including Palantir Maven, to OpenAI, Google and xAI. OpenAI's Feb 27 terms named prohibitions close to Anthropic's two exceptions, so the fight reads as control over who enforces limits, not the limits. Contractors must certify non-use. Consensus reads the Sep 27 dinner as settlement. DoW says the designation stands.

The Jun 12 and Sep 24 actions make foreign access to frontier models a US executive decision. UK AISI, Anthropic's deepest government partner abroad, felt it first. Japan, Australia and Korea MoUs promise shared model information that the same gate can block. This tests the thesis that MoUs are a distribution moat: the record shows no MoU dollars and two US gates.

Pacing advocacy opened a legal channel. The Buist complaint pleads Amodei's Sep 12 essay as evidence of agreement, and the desk's case note expects discovery into any industry working group. Altman endorsed the essay and Musk said Dario is right, and their companies are co-defendants. Consensus reads pacing as brand. The docket reads it as conduct.

The moat case weakens as rivals converge. OpenAI's Chris Lehane opposed SB 53 and an OpenAI-linked PAC network spends over $100M, yet by Sep 2026 OpenAI shared the pacing endorsement, the UN briefing, the White House hold and the FTC probe. When rules bind every large lab, the differentiator is how much discretion the executive applies to each.

Washington access did not insulate. A NAIAC seat (2022), a bipartisan advisory council (Aug 2025), a DC office (Mar 2026) and a PAC (Apr 2026) sit on either side of the Feb 27 ban. The thaw ran through Wiles, Bessent, Lutnick and Trump. New government-affairs hires on Aug 4 and Sep 7 add access; the record shows discretion outweighing it.

watch.item: October international calendar: Australian Senate inquiry hearing in Canberra on Oct 1 (Anthropic named as a safety-practice witness) and the Singapore office opening (12th country)
watch.threshold: Base rate not in the record for foreign-legislature summons; Quartz headline (not opened) says both CEOs skip. A no-show without a written submission signals avoidance of non-US legislatures. Announce-to-open lags in the record: Tokyo 33 days, Sydney 48, Bengaluru 132, Seoul 237; Singapore needs 45 or fewer. A Singapore government MoU would be the sixth.

watch.item: DoD completes removal of Anthropic workloads (Sep 29 or 30 per MeriTalk and FedScoop; end of October per DefenseScoop notes)
watch.threshold: Reference class: this program's own 180-day order from Mar 5 to 6 implied early September; the targets since are Sep 29 or 30 and end of October. A DoD statement of 100% removal confirms the exclusion in practice; residual Claude use (NSA Mythos reports, T3) would show its limits.

watch.item: Appellate path: D.C. Circuit mandate, en banc petition or cert; Ninth Circuit 26-2011 (stayed Apr 27); any government appeal of the Aug 27 judgment
watch.threshold: Base rate for en banc or cert grants is not in the record. Different here: a 2-1 panel with a dissent and a split with N.D. Cal. on causation. A filed petition keeps the legal question open through the IPO; a decision not to seek review closes the track.

watch.item: FTC: formal information demands and compelled testimony from the Sep 30 probe, and the final 'ideological bias' policy statement (proposed Jul 1, 300+ comments)
watch.threshold: One reference class in the record: the FTC AI-partnerships study, orders Jan 2024, report Jan 17, 2025, no enforcement. Different here: executive testimony is planned and Chairman Ferguson's stated view is that developers who instruct agents in cyber tests that cause hacks should be liable. Watch for issued demands that name Anthropic.

watch.item: House 'Great American AI Act' draft (Jun 4): introduction or markup, Anthropic's stated position, and the November midterms
watch.threshold: No base rate for preemption bills in the record. A three-year freeze on state laws on how AI is built could freeze SB 53-type duties; codifying CAISI at $100M a year for 2027 to 2029 is a federal anchor. IPO timing may key off the midterms (Fortune, Yahoo).

watch.item: Sanctions or Entity List action on the six Chinese labs named in advisory AA26-251A (Bessent: 'on the table' Jul 22)
watch.threshold: Ten weeks of threats since Jul 22 with advisory only. A designation of any named firm confirms the export-control and IP thesis; none by year-end means advocacy earned attention, not enforcement.

watch.item: First disclosed paid civil-agency contract after the one-year $1 term that began Aug 12, 2025, or any new DoD-adjacent award
watch.threshold: Base rate not in the record: no paid federal contract is disclosed. A paid renewal shows civil demand survived the ban; none while the DoW exclusion stands would put federal revenue near zero.

watch.item: Mythos 5.1 release to UK AISI after US review, and any White House AI safety board or policy-lead appointment (Trump weighing a 10-person board, Sep 29)
watch.threshold: Release to UK AISI would show the Sep 24 hold was temporary; continued exclusion makes access gating the norm for MoU partners. A board charter would show whether the Sep 29 voluntary pact becomes an institution.

topics.house_view: (a) Extends narrowly: valuation went from $380B at Series G (Feb 12) to $965B at Series H (May 28) through the Pentagon fight, so federal-policy risk carried no visible price, though this slice cannot test multiples. (b) Not tested: federal access runs partly through Bedrock, Vertex and Palantir channels, so any public-sector ARR inherits the gross-versus-net question. (c) Extends: Buist (Sep 18), the D.C. Circuit (Sep 25) and the FTC probe (Sep 30) cluster before pricing, and relayed WSJ reporting names Amodei's risk stance among reasons for a November slip (T3), a timing input that absorption math omits. (d) Not touched by this slice. (e) Confirms: a $200M prototype ceiling that four labs received is not backlog or ARR, and defense-contract conventions do not transfer to SaaS metrics.

uncertainties.note: Federal revenue is not measured in the record. The CDAO agreement has no obligated amount. The several-hundred-million public-sector ARR and the 'hundreds of millions to multiple billions' at-risk range come from a CFO litigation declaration, not audited data. The revenue-mix, customer and prospectus tables are empty.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: Public S-1 disclosure of federal and defense-contractor revenue, or a company statement that quantifies it.

uncertainties.note: Regional revenue is not in the record. Only growth multiples exist: APAC over 10x, EMEA over 9x, India doubled in four months. The offices table also undercounts: Anthropic said 12 cities on Nov 7, 2025 while the table shows 7, Paris, Munich and Dublin opening dates are missing, and London is VERIFY.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: An S-1 geographic revenue note and properties section, or Anthropic office pages.

uncertainties.note: Open conflicts, both sides named. DoD migration: about two-thirds (MeriTalk, T3) versus about 90% (DefenseScoop, T2), with completion Sep 29 or 30 versus end of October. Jun 12 directive: a BIS 'is informed' letter (CSIS, Harvard Law Review Blog) versus an unspecified government directive (Anthropic), and four accounts of the trigger. Sacks: former czar (TechCrunch) versus White House adviser (Sep 13 headline). IL6 and IL7 vendors: seven (TechCrunch) versus eight (CNN).
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: A DoD completion statement, a Commerce or BIS document, or a White House staff listing.

uncertainties.note: Moat versus liability is a judgment, not a measurement. The record has no revenue counterfactual and few regulatory outcomes for OpenAI, Google or xAI. The FTC footnote asymmetry rests on one T3 outlet. The courts split on cause: N.D. Cal. found retaliation, the D.C. Circuit found refusal of 'all lawful uses'.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: Segment revenue disclosure, peer regulatory outcomes, or the FTC statement text.

uncertainties.note: Appeals, FTC and preemption paths are forecasts with no base rate in the record, except one FTC study that took about 12 months and produced no enforcement. What differs here: a 2-1 panel with a dissent, a split with N.D. Cal., and a White House that hosted Amodei on Sep 27 and Sep 29.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: Mandate issuance, a cert or en banc petition, issued FTC demands, or introduced House bill text.

topics.title: People, board and headcount
topics.one_liner: No recorded C-suite exits in 12 months, yet control is redrawn: seven co-founders would get 50.1% of votes on ~2% stakes; the Trust elects 4 of 7 seats.

key_metrics.label: Latest headcount (DISPUTED after Jan 2026)
key_metrics.value: About 2,500 worldwide on Jan 30, 2026 (SFist, T3, single outlet). Mar 2026 T4 estimates: about 3,000 or about 5,000. No T1 or T2 count after Dec 2025.

key_metrics.label: Headcount growth multiple
key_metrics.value: 4.6x (base about 500), 7.7x (about 300), 11.5x or more (under 200): 2,300 in Dec 2025 (Fortune, T2) over a DISPUTED late-2023 base, about 24 months apart.

key_metrics.label: Revenue per employee (two bases, not mixed)
key_metrics.value: Gross run-rate: $3.9M at end-2025 ($9B, company, over 2,300) and $5.6M on Feb 12, 2026 ($14B over 2,500 from Jan 30). Recognized FY2025: $2.0M ($4.6B per leaked prospectus over 2,300).

key_metrics.label: C-suite changes, last 12 months
key_metrics.value: 3 seats changed, all T1 (CTO Oct 2025, CPO Jan 2026, new Chief Global Affairs Officer Aug 2026). 1 more is T4 only (legal). 0 exits on record.

key_metrics.label: Board size
key_metrics.value: 6 directors plus 3 trustees (Reuters factbox, Sep 28, T2). Post-IPO design: 7 seats, Trust elects 4, Class F and Class A holders elect 3.

key_metrics.label: Founder vote at IPO
key_metrics.value: 50.1% of votes via one Class F share. About 2% equity each, about 14% combined (derived). Holds while 3 of 7 keep a minimum stake.

what.t: Headcount points are few and partly disputed. About 40 staff at the Apr 29, 2022 Series B (T1). Late 2023 reads under 200 or about 500 in two Fortune pieces two days apart, and about 300 per Crunchbase (T3). About 2,300 in Dec 2025 (Fortune, T2), about 2,500 on Jan 30, 2026 (SFist, T3). March 2026 aggregator estimates split at about 3,000 and about 5,000 (T4).

Rahul Patil joined as CTO (Oct 7, 2025, T1; TechCrunch Oct 2) and Sam McCandlish became Chief Architect. On Jan 13, 2026 Mike Krieger moved from CPO to co-lead Labs and Ami Vora took Product (T1). Tino Cuéllar became first Chief Global Affairs Officer on Aug 4 (T1). Reuters' Sep 28 factbox lists eight executives: four founders, four hired since May 2024. The record shows no C-suite exits.

Six directors by appointer: founders Dario and Daniela Amodei, investors' seat Yasmin Razavi, Trust Reed Hastings (May 28, 2025) and Vas Narasimhan (Apr 14, 2026), unstated Chris Liddell (Feb 13, 2026). The board grew from four in May 2024 to seven on Apr 14, 2026, a Trust majority (T1). Trust-appointed Jay Kreps reportedly left May 22 (T5, T4 only). Trustees fell to three when Cuéllar left Aug 4.

Reuters (Sep 28, T2) reviewed a leaked draft prospectus. A Founder LLC of seven co-founders directs one Class F share with 50.1% of votes on key matters. The Trust elects four directors; Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei and one other are elected by Class F and Class A holders. The Information, via TechCrunch (Sep 25), adds about 2% each and a three-of-seven minimum-stake test. EDGAR shows no public S-1.

Inbound: Jan Leike (May 2024), John Schulman (Aug 2024), Durk Kingma (Oct 2024), Neil Houlsby from DeepMind (Feb 2025), Andrej Karpathy (May 19, 2026), Dale Finlay from OpenAI (Sep 16, 2026). Schulman left after five months for Mira Murati's startup (T2 relay). Mrinank Sharma (Feb 9, T3) and Jacob Coxon (Sep 8, T2) resigned publicly. Jenny Wen to Cursor rests on a T4 tracker.

Buyback on May 2, 2025: up to 20% of employee shares, $2M per person, two-year tenure, $56.09 a share at $61.5B (T3, single outlet). Tender planned Feb 4, 2026 at $350B pre-money (Bloomberg via aggregator, T3). May 12: Anthropic voided transfers on named secondary platforms (T2). Aug 27: staff may sell inside the IPO and lock-ups may run long (The Information, T4, VERIFY).

means.t: Revenue per head rose because run-rate outran hiring. Run-rate went from about $100M in Sep 2023 (T3, basis unstated) to about $9B at end-2025 (company, gross, T1), roughly 90x, while staff grew 4.6x to at least 11.5x on the disputed base. That is $0.2M-$0.5M per head in late 2023 and $3.9M at end-2025. Recognized FY2025 is $2.0M per head, as recognized revenue trails run-rate in a fast-growing year.

Control sits in two hands. After the IPO the Trust elects 4 of 7 seats. Founders hold 50.1% of votes through Class F, so on this reading they decide the other 3 seats and Class A holders cannot outvote them. Sitting trustees pick new ones with Anthropic, hold no equity, and four of five founding trustees left within 28 months. Post-IPO Class T amendment thresholds are not public.

IPO-readiness hires came in a dated run: CFO Krishna Rao (May 21, 2024), Wilson Sonsini (FT, Dec 2, 2025), ex-Microsoft CFO Chris Liddell to the board (Feb 13, 2026), Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan (Apr 14), confidential S-1 (Jun 1), Cuéllar (Aug 4), legal reshuffle (Aug 26, T4), Matt Clifford (Sep 7, T3). The record ties the policy hires to the Pentagon dispute, so the IPO signal is mixed.

Equity is both the retention lever and the exit risk. Series H ($965B post-money) is 15.7x the May 2025 buyback valuation and 2.6x the tender's pre-money ($900B against $350B). Stock also buys teams: Coefficient Bio, about 10 staff for a reported $400M all-stock, and Runhouse, share-based. The two recorded public resignations cite values, not pay.

implications.t: Hold revenue per head as provisional until the S-1 states headcount. Use $3.9M at end-2025 and $5.6M at Feb 2026, both gross run-rate. The 2,500 versus 5,000 split halves any 2026 figure: annualized Q2 recognized revenue of $46B is $18.4M per head at 2,500 and $9.2M at 5,000. The record has no Q2 headcount.

Treat control as two keys and flag it in both cases. The Trust holds a seat majority by design but has three trustees and, on the best reading, three seated directors today. Founders hold the votes, and the draft warns this could conflict with Class A holders' interests. Price no governance discount until the S-1 shows Class T amendment thresholds, the Class F minimum stake and any sunset.

Rank key-person risk with Daniela Amodei first: Dario Amodei says his only direct report is his chief of staff and all other executives report to her (T3), and she chairs the board. Then Dario Amodei as policy voice, Jared Kaplan (CSO and Responsible Scaling Officer since Oct 2024), Jack Clark (Institute, Mar 11, 2026), Krishna Rao (runs the IPO) and Rahul Patil. Co-founder retention is seven of seven.

Carry employee supply as an unknown, not zero. The record has no lock-up length, no insider-sale size and no stock-compensation figure. Staff may sell inside the offering and lock-ups may exceed the norm (T4, VERIFY). Keep float and overhang as open inputs to the IPO-absorption case until the S-1 states them.

second_order: If the Trust's fourth seat is vacant and Liddell counts as Trust-appointed, the Trust elects three of six today, not a majority. The S-1 board section must show the count. What is easy to miss: the record shows three self-selected trustees, one of whom became an executive, and no Anthropic statement of the split after Apr 14.

Two public resignations on safety grounds (Feb 9, Sep 8), the second 20 days before the leaked prospectus, bracket RSP v3.4 (Jul 8), which cut mandatory sharing of unredacted Risk Reports to at least 200 employees. The record shows no link. S-1 drafters must word key-personnel and dissent risk with care. Liquidity alone will not hold staff whose stated reason is values.

Staff who sold in the tender at $350B pre-money sold at about 39% of the May Series H pre-money, and the IPO is reported at $2T or more. Lock-up expiry, not the IPO, becomes the retention test. Anthropic must carry staff past that date; the record holds no vesting or refresh-grant data and names no outbound move to OpenAI.

Fortune's seven co-founders omit Ben Mann, whom Anthropic's Labs post calls a co-founder, and prospectus coverage does not list the seven. If Mann sits outside the Founder LLC, a Labs co-lead is outside the control bloc. The S-1's named Founder LLC members settle it.

Two UK appointments, Rishi Sunak (Oct 9, 2025) and Matt Clifford (Sep 7, 2026), drew conflict-of-interest questions, and Clifford stays ARIA chair until Nov 6. The D.C. Circuit upheld the FASCSA exclusion on Sep 25. A policy arm staffed between Aug 4 and Sep 7 may face related-party and adviser disclosure in the S-1.

watch.item: Public S-1 filed on EDGAR (none as of Sep 30)
watch.threshold: No filing by Oct 31 pushes the listing past the WSJ November target (Sep 18). Every item below is first read here.

watch.item: S-1 employee count with an as-of date
watch.threshold: 4,000 or more supports the T4 estimate of about 5,000; 3,000 or less supports the lean reading. Either sets revenue per head.

watch.item: S-1 executive officers and executive compensation
watch.threshold: Whether Tom Brown (Chief Compute Officer), Jack Clark and the Labs co-leads are executive officers; the factbox as summarized lists eight and omits them. Any large equity award to Rao, Patil, Smith or Ciauri.

watch.item: S-1 board section: seated Trust directors, Kreps exit, Liddell's appointer, successor for Cuéllar's trustee seat
watch.threshold: Four Trust-elected directors seated before pricing is a majority of 7; three of 6 is not. A fourth trustee named ends the three-person Trust. Any independent chair, lead director or audit committee chair, since Daniela Amodei is President and Board Chair.

watch.item: Founder LLC and Class T terms, plus shareholder approval of the Class F structure
watch.threshold: Minimum stake per founder, any sunset, who can amend Class T, and whether the Series C investors' seat held by Yasmin Razavi survives. The approval date is not in the record.

watch.item: Lock-up length and selling holders in the prospectus
watch.threshold: A lock-up longer than the market norm (The Information, T4, VERIFY), any employee shares sold inside the offering, and the size of insider sales.

watch.item: Senior departures before pricing
watch.threshold: Any exit among the eight listed executives, the seven co-founders or the three trustees (none on record for 12 months), or a third public resignation on safety grounds.

watch.item: Matt Clifford leaves the ARIA chair
watch.threshold: Date slips past Nov 6 or UK conflict-of-interest scrutiny escalates beyond the Labour MP's question (The Register, T3).

topics.house_view: (a) Valuation-quality paradox: extends, cannot test; the slice adds a quality datapoint, $3.9M gross run-rate per head at end-2025, but the record has no peer headcount and the comparables table is empty. (b) Equalization ruling: extends; revenue per head inherits Anthropic's gross basis, which OpenAI contests (Apr 13, T2), so any peer comparison needs the same equalization first. (c) IPO absorption: extends; staff selling inside the offering and lock-up length are supply inputs with no figures in the record (T4, VERIFY). (d) Capital efficiency: extends; the record does not say whether tender purchases used company cash or new-round money, so equity raised may partly fund liquidity rather than operations. (e) Sector conventions: extends; founder super-voting precedents (Meta, Snap) do not map one-to-one here, where control is collective, stakes are about 2% each and a purpose Trust elects the seat majority.

uncertainties.note: Headcount after Dec 2025 has no T1 or T2 source: 2,500 (T3, Jan), about 3,000 and about 5,000 (T4, Mar). The desk's canonical 5,000 for Apr 21 carries no URL. The late-2023 base is under 200, about 300 or about 500. Prospectus coverage opened reports no headcount.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: An S-1 employee count with an as-of date, or an Anthropic statement.

uncertainties.note: Board and roster are not settled. Kreps's May 22 exit rests on T5 and T4 sources, and Liddell's appointing body is unstated; both decide whether the Trust kept a seat majority after Apr 14. Start dates for CLO Brian Israel, Chief People Officer Hannah Pritchett and Chief Brand and Communications Officer Sasha de Marigny are not in the record, so the count of 3 C-suite changes may be understated. The record also names no audit-committee chair, investor-relations head or chief accounting officer.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: Anthropic's board and leadership pages with dates, the S-1 board section, or a T2 report on Kreps.

uncertainties.note: The post-IPO balance of control is read from two accounts. Reuters gives seats and votes but not amendment thresholds, the Class F minimum stake, a sunset or the fate of the investor-elected seat. The third Class F and Class A seat is a founder seat per The Information and one unnamed director per Reuters. The 2% stakes come from one outlet relayed by TechCrunch. Which seven co-founders sit in the Founder LLC is not stated: Fortune's seven omit Ben Mann, and the factbox as summarized omits Tom Brown.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: The S-1 charter summary and the Founder LLC agreement.

uncertainties.note: Employee supply at and after the IPO cannot be sized. Lock-up base rates are not in the record. The nearest comparable, SpaceX's June 2026 IPO, had no secondary component (The Information, T4). Here staff may sell inside the offering and lock-ups may run long (T4, VERIFY). Buyback and tender terms are single-source T3, and the tender's final size and take-up are headline-only.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: The S-1 sections on shares eligible for future sale and on equity plans.

uncertainties.note: Talent flow is selectively recorded. The record is built around Anthropic events, so named inbound hires with OpenAI ties (five) are over-covered and outbound moves under-covered. FREED, a T4 tracker, is sole source for Jenny Wen's move and a co-source for Kreps and Schulman's destination. Two public resignations are not an attrition rate.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: A turnover figure in the S-1 or alumni data from a second source.
